utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hannis, just a comment about yesterday afternoon before we proceed today. The Trial Chamber has carefully reviewed the evidence of Mrs. Rrahmani, and having done so can see that the way in which this was presented was clearly aimed at clarifying the identity of armed groups whom the witness observed, and in the opinion of the Trial Chamber, it is perfectly appropriate to present a statement and to seek clarification of parts of the statement or even to seek to emphasise parts of the statement, and it's also appropriate to bring out new material from a witness if proper notification of that material has been given to the Defence. However, it won't serve the purpose of clarifying the evidence in a written statement if the Chamber have difficulty following the way in which it sought to present the clarification, and we did think we had already made it clear that we would like you to identify the parts of the statement to which the clarification that's being sought relates, and I think that was the problem yesterday, that we weren't kept abreast of the progress that was being made through the statement. It is important to bear in mind that you know your case much better than we do, and we would be grateful if in future you could assist us and those working with you could assist us by identifying the parts of the statement to which the questions are directed. In the end of the day, it took much more effort than should be necessary to see that what you were doing was a perfectly reasonable and proper exercise of the time that you have to lead evidence viva voce.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I thank you for those remarks, Your Honour, and we'll be guided by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, who is the next witness, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, our next witness is Sadije Sadiku.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, could you please make the solemn declaration by reading allowed the document which has been placed in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Sadiku, the Chamber already have a statement in writing which you previously gave. Now we're at the stage where we are going to hear further evidence from you in answer to questions that will be put by counsel for the Prosecution and for the Defence. It's very important when dealing with these questions for you to concentrate on the question that is being asked and to answer that particular question, because we already have a very full account of your evidence before us, and what parties are trying to do is identify parts that they either wish more information about or that they may wish to challenge. And don't be surprised if someone challenges your evidence because that's just part of the process that's followed in this Tribunal to try to seek out -- to seek out the truth, which is the job we are trying to do. So please bear with the system, face up to the questions, and answer each specific question put to you as briefly as you possibly can. The first counsel to ask questions of you will be, on behalf of the Prosecution, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you state for the record, please, your name.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. My name is Sadije Sadiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And Ms. Sadiku, you are an Albanian Muslim born in Mitrovica in 1978, and you were raised in the Kosovo Albanian village of Zhabar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I should indicate that we're proceeding this witness as an 89(F) witness, and at this time I would like to pull up Exhibit P2256 and hand the witness hard copy of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, could you take a look at that document in front of you and tell us whether or not you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that a statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor earlier this week?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you confirm for the Judges that -- whether or not that statement is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 2256 at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, this is a statement which plainly falls within the provisions of 89(F). The Chamber's already indicated that it welcomes this approach to the presentation of evidence, and this becomes part of the record in the case, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, your village was located very near the town of Mitrovica in Mitrovica municipality?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How big a town was that, or village, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It had about 5, 600 houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, your written statement, as the Judge just said, will be part of the evidence in this case, so I want to quickly take you through your statement. In paragraph 11, you talk about how on the 13th of April, 1999, police started to expel villagers and burn houses in one end of the village. How did you know about that at the time? Did you see it yourself or did you hear it?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what did you and your family do when you realised this was happening?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: As soon as we saw that they started to torch the houses, we left our home and went to the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in your statement you tell us you spent the night out in the cold and rain, and the next morning, on the 14th, you returned to your house; in paragraphs 13 and 14. Why did you go back to your house on the 14th? Weren't you worried about the police?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Even though we were worried about the police and it was very cold and raining, we had to go back because there was nothing we had to eat, that's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you describe then what happened on that morning. The police kicked you out at gunpoint, telling you if you didn't leave in five minutes they would kill you. Did they tell you why you had to leave your home?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: When they entered our home, they shot -- they fired -- excuse me. They trained their arms at us and told us to leave the house in five minutes and leave also Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you going to try again on that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But did they give you explanation about why you had to leave? Did they tell you why?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell us why we had to leave the houses, but they threatened us, and we didn't dare remain there any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, in paragraphs 16 through 20 of your statement, you describe how you were part of a column of approximately 8.000 people and how you were walking for two days and nights to get to Klina e Eperme. What was the ethnicity of those people in your column of 8.000?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Generally Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say generally Albanians. Do you know what the other people were who were not Albanians in that group?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The answer appears on the transcript as, "Generally Albanians." Does that mean that there were some non-Albanians in that group of 8.000?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: As far as our convoy where I was, all of us were Albanians, people from Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, when you left in that convoy, did you know where you were going to go?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. No, we didn't know. That was the first time for me to travel in that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know what was going to happen to you?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, if we could -- I would like to put up a map. It's Exhibit P39.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, I don't know if you can see this on your screen.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. Now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we scroll up and to the right. Near the top of that map, can you see -- if we zoom in a little bit, can you see where your village is located?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where did you go when you left that morning, the 14th of April? Do you remember the first place you went?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. This is Shipol here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then in your statement you say after going to Shipol you went on toward Klina e Eperme, and the men joined you at a location called Lushta, if I'm pronouncing that correctly.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There's a pen on the table in front of you I think you can use to draw on the map in front of you. I'll have the usher help you. If you could for the Judges, first of all could you draw a circle around your home village of Zhabar.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next if you could draw a circle around Shipol.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then Lushta where the men joined you.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, if we could scroll up on the map and over to the left. Oh, I'm sorry. Do I need to take a screen shot of this one --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Before we do that, could we take a screen shot of this and have this marked as the next IC.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be IC9, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, could we scroll up on this map and move slightly to the left. Or I guess -- I'm sorry, scroll down and move slightly to the left. Ms. Sadiku, if you'd bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from -- from there where did you end up after two days and nights of walking? The name of the town?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: After two days and nights of walking, we arrived in Klina e Begut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: We arrived in Klina e Begut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In your statement I have it written down as Klina e Eperme. Are they the same thing?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. No, they are two different places. Klina e Eperme is near Skenderaj. Klina e Begut is another place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you able to locate that on this map?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I see here only Klina e Mesme which is in the vicinity of Skenderaj. We arrived here at this place, Klina e Mesme. I don't see Klina e Begut in this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is Klina e Mesme near -- I'm sorry, the location you named, is it close to any location you can see on the map in front of you? If you know.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It is difficult to find things on a map, because for me, as I said, it was the first time to pass through that place. That's why it's difficult to pinpoint it in the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's all right. We'll pass on that. I won't ask you to make any marks on that map, then. If we could show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, there's some uncertainty, though, about that answer, because while it rules out Klina e Eperme, there was reference to Klina e Mesme, and it says, "We arrived here at this place, Klina e Mesme, I don't see on this map." Now that's confusing, because Klina e Mesme is on the map, and it's not clear to me that the witness wants to say she went there. Could we have that clarified and then find out in which direction from her home the place is that she actually went to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will try, Your Honour, and I guess I misheard the answer about Klina e Mesme.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First of all, Ms. Sadiku, can you tell us whether or not you arrived at Klina e Mesme at any time during this trip?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And was that before or after you reached the location that you've now described as Kline e Begut?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, was it before you reached it or after you reached Kline e Begut?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Before we went to Kline e Begut, there is Klina e Mesme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's much clearer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, if we could go and show you Exhibit P32. And if we could zoom in on the area south of Istok. A little farther to the right. I'm sorry. Yes, scroll up. A little further. Thank you. And zoom in in that bottom right corner. Thank you. In your statement, in paragraph 20, again it makes reference to a location called Klina e Eperme. Did you go through or stop at a location known as Klina e Eperme?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. We were in a convoy, a long convoy of people when we went through the Klina e Eperme.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The convoy did go through that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in your statement in page [sic] 20 you say that's the location where the column was divided, with some 2.000 of the people being told to go back, and you and the remaining 6.000 were to continue onwards; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where did you and your group of 6.000 go to then after the convoy was split? What's the next location you remember the name of?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you need to look at your statement to refresh your memory about the name of the location?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If at any time you need to do that, please let us know that you're looking at that document instead of talking about from what's inside your head. Have you had a chance?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And does that --

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And does that refresh your memory about where you went next?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. We went in the direction of Peja.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in paragraph 21 and 22, you tell us about where you stayed on the third night of your exodus out of Kosovo, where you were finally allowed to rest, and paragraph 22, you describe how the next morning you continued towards a village called Zablace, if I'm pronouncing that correctly. Can you tell us -- well, first of all, can you look at the map that's on the screen in front of you now.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you able to see the village of Zabac on that?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you use the pen again and draw a circle around Zabac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we scroll up a little bit before I have her mark on that because there's another location we'd like to include. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First of all, could you draw a circle around Zabac.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 23 of your statement, Ms. Sadiku, you tell us how your group of about 6.000 were told by the police to make accommodation in that village. Was there anyone already living there when you arrived at that location?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. There were no people there, only shelled houses, but no people.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you tell us in your statement that -- in paragraphs 23 and 24, how the police told you to stay there until further notice and that you had to try to arrange yourself as best you could in those deserted houses. In paragraphs 32 to 39 -- I'm sorry. Let me stop there for a minute. During those three weeks, what did you live on in terms of food?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: During these three weeks we had nothing to eat other than some potatoes we could find.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then at the end of three weeks, on the 6th of May, could you just briefly tell the Judges what happened to you that day?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: On the 6th of May, at 8.00 in the morning, I left the house where we were staying and went out to find something to eat. I was together with some other friends. We went, got the food, and came back. On the way back, I was together with a friend and we were carrying a sack. At that moment, we felt tired because the sack was very heavy, and my friend said, "Let's exchange hands." And I wanted to turn back and catch the sack with the other hand, but at that moment I felt a pain on my back and fell down on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: My friend left me crying, and I personally didn't know what had happened to me. I started to look about my body to try to understand what the problem was because I didn't hear the shot. And then on my chest I saw that blood was coming out, and then I removed the clothes to see what was the problem there, and I saw a big wound on my right side, and then I dropped my clothes, was scared, and cried out for help. But when the police saw that I was moving, they started to shoot again at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were your sisters eventually able to come out and drag you inside the house?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. For half an hour, nobody came to my rescue and dragged me from that place because there was constant shooting and firing in my direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But after a half hour, eventually they got you inside the house?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. We were waiting for the shots to stop, but they continued. So my sister -- my sisters came out from the house and dragged me from that place irrespective of the bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As a result of that injury have you been paralysed and in a wheelchair since that time?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Ever since that date, the 6th of May, 1999, I am in this wheelchair.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, Ms. Sadiku, you tell us how -- well, you describe what was done to try and treat you and how you were moved to another location, to a village called Zahac. On the map in front of you, can you see where Zahac is located?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you draw a circle around that for us, please, with that pen.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's another one on the map but we're quite sure that's the right one? There's one nearer Pec as well. THE PROSECUTOR: There is one nearer Pec, near the railroad line, and I don't know which is the correct one and I don't know if the witness does, or if she can assist, because I'm not sure of my pronunciation or the correct Albanian spelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, do you see on the map as you move from Zabac toward Peja along the railroad line below it there is another Zahac indicated? Do you know whether the circle you've just drawn or that Zahac would be the one you talk about in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I think this -- the one I have surrounded near Zabac, because it was that place. Where this happened was not far from Zabac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you described your journey out of Kosovo after that. Could we have that -- I'm sorry, a screen shot taken of that and give it to the next IC number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC10, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then in your statement, I believe in paragraphs 32 through 39, you describe the route you took before you eventually arrived in Albania, passing through Decane, Gjakova, Prizren and Zhur?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Zhur. It's called Zhur.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 38, Ms. Sadiku, you describe how when you reached the border, the border police demanded money. Which side of the border are we talking about? Is that on the Kosovo side of the border or on the Albanian side of the border?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I am talking about the Kosovar side of the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the border police, what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: They were Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What kind of uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Dark blue uniforms and some had black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you say in that paragraph that all your IDs were seized. Did -- can you tell us anything else about that? What happened with your IDs or your identity documents after they were taken from you?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: They stopped us at this checkpoint, asked for money and for the IDs, passports, whatever we had on us. The person -- whoever who had the document gave the documents to the guards, and they tore them up and burned them. Those who didn't have documents on them were beaten up and then they left quickly, as far as they could. They were maltreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see that with your own eyes as far as what happened to the documents? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, lastly, I want to ask you concerning your injury from the gunshot wound. Do you still suffer any pain as a result of that?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I have pain. I have a lot of problems. So far I have undergone 10 surgeries, and there is another one pending. Once I return from here, I will undergo another operation in Kosova, and I need to have another surgery done on my back, but for the moment in Kosova this kind of operation is not performed by the doctors there, cannot be performed, but I cannot afford to go to some other place to have it done, so I don't know what will happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is my understanding correct that the last surgery you described is one that might enable you to walk again?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. The fact is that if I undergo another surgery on my backbone in someplace outside Kosova, maybe I can walk again. But my problem is that I cannot afford to pay for the operation, and this is the reason why I have to remain in this condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no questions. The order will be General Lazarevic, General Lukic, General Pavkovic, Mr. Sainovic, and General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Sadiku, my name is Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney-at-law, one of the counsel for General Vladimir Lazarevic. Before I start asking you questions, I wanted to express my regret for you having suffered the injuries you have. I will have but a few questions for you to try and clarify certain things. Ms. Sadiku, on the 6th of May, 1999, at 8.00, you were injured; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: After the injury, as far as I understand, a physician came from Mitrovica by the name of Shaqir Demiri and he checked your condition; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. Shaqir Demiri didn't come from Mitrovica to visit me. He was in the convoy with us during all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. And he checked your condition?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: He only measured my blood pressure. He couldn't do much for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: He took your blood pressure and that was it?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. He only took my blood pressure, because he couldn't do much more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: After that you were transferred to the village of Zahac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the village of Zahac you were also assisted by someone as regards some sort of care given to you?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what sort of assistance did you receive in that village?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: The assistance I received is surprising, I would say, in the sense that they only looked at my wound without giving me any anaesthetic or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I understood correctly, Ms. Sadiku, the next four days, you spent that at the village itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: After that, on the fifth day, you joined the convoy which went across Decane, Djakovica, Prizren, and Zhur towards Albania; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And how long did it take for you to reach the destination?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It took us a long time, but I cannot give you a precise estimate because I was in a very bad condition, and I was lying in that state without eating anything, without receiving any assistance for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Miss, you will agree perhaps if I said that the journey took over one day?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, more than one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And on the 12th of May, 1999, you crossed a border to Albania at the village of Kukes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And due to serious internal haemorrhaging, the very same day or the next day you were transferred to the Albanian military hospital in Tirana. Therefore, I would like to know whether that was on that same day or the next day.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: This happened on the same day we entered Kukes, on that very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, among the documents we received from the OTP there are some documents originating from the central military hospital in Tirana. We received your case history, where it is stated that you were admitted into the hospital on the 8th of May, 1999 and that you sustained a gunshot injury three days before you were admitted. Can you explain the discrepancy between your statement and the official document issued by the central military hospital, which we received from the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The date is a problem because the doctor who wrote the case history made the mistake on the date of my admittance to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know of that detail earlier or is it only now that you were able to recollect? Did I jog your memory perhaps by the question I put?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I knew this earlier, but there was nothing I could do about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Couldn't you have explained that to the OTP, to draw their attention to that since you were proofed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, only if she were asked about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed. I don't understand the question, Mr. Bakrac. You're asking about a mistake which has no -- if in fact it is a mistake, it's immaterial to the case. If the 12th is the right date, then all this doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will have a follow-up question, and then you will be able to see my position better perhaps. I'm trying to establish what the truth is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, on the 3rd of July, 1999, you were transferred at the Emergency Ward in Murnau in Germany; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, in the case history issued by that hospital, it is stated, and I will quote a sentence: "Ms. Sadiku suffered a gunshot injury in abdominal area and the lumbar part of the spine on the 5th of July, 1999."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The 5th of June, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: -- "In Kosovo-Albania." Which is correct: Were you injured on the 5th or the 6th of May or perhaps on the 5th of June in Albania, Ms. Sadiku?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I was injured on the 6th of May. That is the day when I was injured. With respect to the doctor's case histories, I have no information of that. I don't know what they have written on them. The fact is that I was, as I said, injured on the day that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ma'am. My name is Dan Ivetic, and together with my colleagues Branko Lukic and Ozren Ogrizovic, I represent Mr. Sreten Lukic today, and today it is my job to ask you some questions to better understand the events that you witnessed in Kosovo-Metohija during the relevant time period for these proceedings. I apologise in advance if my questions cause you to recall upsetting moments of your life. In fact, we intended to limit our cross-examination but given the new statement that the Prosecutor elicited from you the other day, I'm obliged to ask some questions to clear up areas that I otherwise would not have gone into. I would only ask that you pay close attention to what I ask you and try to limit your answers to what I specifically ask, and we'll try to get through this as quickly as possible. Are you ready to begin, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my first question, Ms. Sadiku, in 1998 and 1999, did you speak or understand the Serbian or Serbo-Croatian language?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now I want to ask you a couple of questions to try and clear up in my own mind the statements -- the allegations made in your various statements to the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, and first of all, I'd like to focus on your statement of the 23rd of August, 2001, which I believe is Exhibit P2252 in e-court. Now, do you recall giving this statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you, was this statement read back to you in verbatim in the Albanian language at the conclusion of your interview?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And after this statement was read to you, you in fact signed the -- the English version of at that statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you signed that statement, it was explained to you that you were certifying that each paragraph set forth in the statement was true to the best of your knowledge and recollection; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were you in fact given a copy of the statement after it was completed, in Albanian or in any other language?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And for the time period of August, 2001, through August 15, 2006, just really this week, for approximately five years you did not make any objection to the statement from August of 2001 or amend it in any way. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: That is correct, because there were some things not very clear because of translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you'll agree with me that the statement you gave to the Prosecutor on August 15, 2006, that is the most recent statement, that statement is not identical to the one you gave in 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: That is correct. As I said, this is due to some unclarities of translation. After I read it in Albania, I came to this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And when did you read the statement in Albanian to come to this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I read it. I don't remember the exact date. I read it three, four days after I came here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So in any event, sometime perhaps this week or last week. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: This week, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's focus on the time period before then. Between the time that you first gave your statement in 2001 to the Office of the Prosecutor and when you came here in the past week to go over it, did you discuss or go over that statement with anybody else?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. Between the time period you first gave your statement in 2001 and this past week when you came here to go over it and to testify, in that intervening time period did you discuss your statement or go over your statement with anybody else?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to repeat your question again, because it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. No problem. Between August of 2001 and August 15th of 2006, did you go over or discuss with anybody else the statement that you gave in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. I take it, then, that -- well, let me ask you. Did anyone encourage or influence you to change portions of your testimony as set out in your written statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No, no. Everything that is there is given out of my free will. Whatever is changed, I did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And focusing now on this statement, let's focus on the statement from August 2001 for the sake of clarity -- do you have a copy of that statement in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a hard copy we could provide to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If counsel could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is in the system but not in Albanian. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is, but I think if he is going to direct her to specific paragraphs it may be easier for her to work from a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I have handwritten numbered paragraphs on that copy she has, just for counsel's information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll keep that in mind, although since I don't -- I don't know which paragraphs those would be, but I do have -- I do have fairly precise page and paragraph references that I have come up with, so hopefully we'll be able to follow. Can I proceed, Your Honour, or was there -- should I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, focusing at this -- on this statement, in the Albanian version at page 3, paragraph 3, in English it's page 3, paragraph 2, and in B/C/S it's page 3 and the first paragraph. In that portion of the statement, ma'am, this statement from 2001 states that the police came to your house "many times," and that on one occasion that you specifically remembered they shot a burst of fire in the ground and you said, "We were only women and children at the house at that time." And the statement goes on to state that you recognised one of the police that was present. Now, this portion of your 2001 statement explicitly states that you were presence for this occurrence and that you were an eyewitness to the same, does it not?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, isn't that what this paragraph of the August 2001 statement indicates, that you remembered an event, I mean I could read the whole thing: "I can remember once where we were about 80 people in the house. They shot a burst of fire on the ground and threatened us, to kill us all unless we gave them money and jewelleries. They also slapped a small girl. We were only women and children in the house at the time." This paragraphs indicates that you were present when this event occurred, does it not?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No, I wasn't present there. This happened after we were driven out of the house and I heard about this event. I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand that, ma'am, and I'm going to get to that. But this statement from 2001, it indicates that you were present for this event, does it not?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question a different way, ma'am. Is this part of your statement from 2001 inaccurate in its description of how you know about this event?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: This part is accurate, but the only problem is that I was not present there to see it myself. I heard it from someone else. I wasn't present. I only heard about this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in this part of the statement it is alleged that the police shot into the ground, and I believe even the new statement that you -- that you signed just the other day continues to allege that the police shot into the ground and there are holes in the wall to this day. Isn't that another inconsistency in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not clear to me what that answer means, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's not to me either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So I don't think you should skip on thinking it was in agreement with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, your statement claims that the police shot into the ground, and when we use the term -- well, let me put it to you this way: The bullet holes that you allege are still -- still present or at least were still present in your home at the time of the statement, are they in the ground or are they in the wall of the home?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: They are on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So would it be accurate to state, then, that the part of the statement that alleges that the holes are in the wall of the home is another inaccuracy of this statement?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. Let me ask it a different way and maybe it will come out clearer in the translation. Is the part of the statement signed for the Prosecutor's office that claims that the bullet holes were in the wall, is that another example of where this statement differs from the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now I'm confused, Your Honour. Which statement are we talking about? Because if he says it's another example where this statement differs from the truth, I thought we only had one example from the statement in 2001 and one or none from the statement in 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought we were talking about the statement from 2001, if I could perhaps limit myself to that at this portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, is that allegation in this statement from 2001 that the bullet holes were in the wall not, in fact, true?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I have a reference to where in the 2001 statement there's a reference to holes in the wall?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. That's the 2006 statement. That's the problem, when they're both identical in most regards. I apologise. That's probably where the confusion comes in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The 2006 statement, at the paragraph that is labelled number 9, which is on page 3 of the English. Unfortunately, I cannot say what page of the Albanian since it was not given to us. Does it not state there, ma'am, that the bullet marks are still on the wall? Do I need to repeat the question or --

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that the bullet holes are still there on the floor of the house where they shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So then is -- is that part of the statement that claims the bullet marks are on the wall inaccurate is all that I'm trying to find out before I can move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't need that question to be answered by the witness, Mr. Ivetic. You've made the point you seek to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, you indicated that you were not present for this particular incident. Would it be fair to say, then, that you have no way of knowing what kind of uniforms these individuals described as police were wearing? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: At what time? Can you please specify it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. This incident that we discussed that is alleged in paragraph 9 of your 2006 statement and which is alleged at page 3, paragraph 3 of your 2001 statement where it is alleged that the individuals came in and shot their weapons into the ground. For this incident, since you were not there, you have no way of knowing what types or kinds of uniforms these individuals who did this were wearing. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: That is correct. Since I wasn't there present, there is no way how I can describe the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And since you were not personally present, you have no way to confirm whether the details of this incident as told to you by other people are accurate. Isn't that also correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: That is correct. Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. There's no need to repeat it because it's stating the obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at page 4 of the Albanian version, again of your 2001 statement, and paragraph 4 of that statement, that's page 3, paragraph 4 of the English, and page 3, paragraph 4 of the B/C/S, you cite to 80 people that were staying with your family at that time after you had left your village, after you had left your house in the forest. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. This is accurate. I realised it after the war that about 80 people were in our home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And on the third paragraph on that page in the Albanian, page 3, paragraph 6 of the English version and page 3, paragraph 6 of the B/C/S, you state that after that, on April 14, 1999, a group of seven police came to your house and you and these same 80 people that were cited previously were ordered out of the house and told to go "wherever you want to go, Albania or somewhere else." Isn't that what you statement of 2001 indicates? And if you need to take some time to read that paragraph, by all means do so.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we turn to that same paragraph of your new statement, that is to say the statement from August 15th of 2006, that would be paragraph number 14 in that statement -- I'm assuming that the English paragraphs are the same as the Albanian, Mr. Hannis. Thank you. So in paragraph 14 of your new statement from August the 15th, 2006, we see that the -- your testimony relating to this event has been modified and changed so that rather than 80 people being present, you now state that there were approximately 20 people there. Is that -- is that one change in your testimony between these two statements?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It is a change, because on the 13th of April, we were 80 persons in my home. Fifty persons came from Qirez. I say 80. I couldn't give you an accurate figure, but on the 30th -- 13th of April, we left home, and those 50 persons from Qirez went in another direction. I don't know which direction they went. And the remainder, around 20, were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And another difference between your two statements is now in terms of how you describe the activities of the persons who you label as the police, in the newest version of your statement, the August 2006 version, the police do not give you the option to go wherever you want to go, to Albania or somewhere else, they direct you to the roadway. Is that accurate -- or does that accurately reflect what your testimony as contained in the August 15, 2006 statement, what that is?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: This is very accurate what I said; namely, that those policemen who came to our house ordered us that we leave the house in five minutes. When we went outside in the street, there were other policemen there telling us something else. That is why we were confused. We didn't know where to go. Some told us one thing; some others told us another thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So would it be safe to say, then, ma'am, that this statement from 2006, which purports to show your testimony in this case, is that it does not include everything that people told you on that day? It's not a complete picture. Is that what you're trying to tell me?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Whatever I have said is contained in these pages. I don't know what you want me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking if in fact -- well, strike that. I think the documents speak for themselves. Now, earlier you told me that you do not -- that you neither speak nor understand the Serbian language. How is it, then, that you understood what these individuals that you label as policemen were saying and telling you?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Even though I didn't understand the language, didn't speak the language, but my mother and my elder sister, they knew the language. They spoke it. So they understood and told me what all this was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, then, that throughout your statement wherever you cite to something that an alleged Serbian police officer said, would it be fair to say that those statements are based secondhand upon what somebody else told you that those individuals said?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That assume facts in evidence. The Serbian policeman may have spoken to her in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, the witness has been given an opportunity to explain her knowledge, and she's explained it. Carry on, Mr. Ivetic. There's nothing wrong with that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do I need to -- I'll read it back for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, then, that throughout your statement wherever you cite to something that an alleged Serbian police officer cited, would it be fair to say that those statements are based secondhand upon what somebody else told you that those individuals said?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I don't know where you want to get at, sir. I'm telling you that everything -- most of the things I have stated in my statement I have seen with my own eyes. There are very minor things which I report to have heard from others.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was hoping to shortcut some of my questions but I guess I'll have to ask you about each time that you spoke with a police officer. In any event, let's focus and finish up with this incident on the 14th of April, first of all. Can you please describe for us what kind of uniforms these people who came into your house were wearing?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. They were wearing dark blue and black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia or badges?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. When they entered the house, we didn't have time to look carefully at their uniforms and their insignia. They threatened us, so we didn't dare look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And did these individuals arrive in any type of vehicles?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: They came in vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I can direct your attention, I believe it's on the same page, paragraph 9 of your most recent statement, you earlier stated that the police came in blue vehicles called Pinzgauers. Is the term "Pinzgauer" something that you knew at the time as a technical term for the specific type of vehicle, or is that something that someone else told you relative to the technical nature of the vehicles that you viewed?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No, no one told me the names, but we knew that there were such vehicles, such specific vehicles called Pinzgauers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, moving ahead to the time period when you were in the convoy of people. At page 5, paragraph 3 of the Albanian version of your original 2001 statement. That's page 4 and paragraph 6 of the English, page 4, paragraph 5 of the B/C/S. I'll give you some time to get to there. In that paragraph you state that in Klina e Eperme many women were ripped of their earrings direct without possibility to take them off by themselves, and then you identify one policeman that did this. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact, in your new statement from 2006, I believe at paragraph 20 of that statement, you have now clarified your testimony that in fact you only saw this happen to three or four women; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, there was only one policeman that you describe as having done this. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: That is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you -- can you describe the uniform that this individual was wearing?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: The uniform I described earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Plain colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you acknowledge in both statements that another policeman who heard about this conduct identified the perpetrator as a bandit and went off to find him. Did you take that to mean that the action of ripping earrings off of women was viewed as a criminal act by this second policeman and that they considered the man who did that a bandit, a criminal?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that calls for speculation on the part of this witness. There could be all kinds of reasons he told her that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking for her impression based upon the acts that she witnessed. I mean, how did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This -- I'm beginning to despair of some of this, Mr. Ivetic. I mean, you're asking the witness to state what I've already said is the obvious. It's a matter for us in due course to draw a conclusion from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough. Thank you, Your Honour. Should I proceed to another area of questioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Actually, in her statement she had explained categorically that when that was pointed out that this fellow has ripped the earring, it was said that he was a bandit and he went away, which of course implies that both were hand in glove, and I think this question was rather -- was quite vague and confusing and misleading, please. I apologise using these words. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As I indicated, I will move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When the convoy, as you testified, was split, would you describe the -- again, you state it's a policeman on a motorcycle. What was his uniform like?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: The same uniform I referred to earlier, and there was only one policeman who told the convoy to split, and that happened in Klina e Eperme.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now again I have to ask you about this police officer who spoke to the persons in the convoy. Did he speak in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And therefore, I take it your knowledge of what he said is based secondhand upon what someone else told you he said. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. I take it your knowledge of what he said is based secondhand upon what someone else told you that he said. Is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I already told you that even though I don't speak and understand Serbian, it's my mother and my elder sisters who understood everything what was going on. They explained to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, my next line of questioning is, unfortunately, going to have to turn to examine the events relating to the date when you were injured, and again I apologise if this is an upsetting topic, but there are some apparent inconsistencies I have to go through to try and ascertain what happened. So please bear that in mind and try not to take my questions in a negative light. Now, first of all, the -- your initial statement from 2001 does not mention that you were accompanied by anyone when you left where you were staying to go find -- I believe it was the potatoes, prior to being shot. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It is true that I wasn't alone. I can't tell you for sure whether we were seven or eight friends, but the fact is we were a group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But you will concede that that is not set forth in your statement of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Ivetic, why you need to ask that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to ascertain whether the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I mean, I've got the statement in front of me. I can see it's not in it. So why is it you need to ask that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I need to know whether the problems or inconsistencies in the statement are something related to the witness or related to the process in which the statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But why do you need her to concede that it's not in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm willing to stipulate that it's not.

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: You know --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it is obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But answer my question. Why is it you need her to concede that it's not in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Because I'm trying to find out from talking to her to understand how it is that the statements differ so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But getting her to concede it's not there, how does that advance your case? I just want to understand that one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That answer by itself may not, but other answers I may elicit may, and so I'm trying to deal with this in a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: With great respect to you, Mr. Ivetic, you seem to ask an awful lot of questions that are confusing for this witness, and I, for my part, find most of them quite unnecessary. So please try and focus the cross-examination so that you ask necessary questions and don't ask questions to which the answer to obvious to the Bench. Now, we'll take our break there, and we will resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, this afternoon you've talked about the police wearing dark blue uniforms. I would ask you, were all of the police officers we have discussed up until date, the alleged police officers, were they wearing single-colour uniforms or were their uniforms consisting of patterns or colours?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: The ones that I saw had the colour I mentioned earlier. But at the same time, there were soldiers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me focus you in on the police officer that you stated was on a motorcycle. In addition to his uniform, did he have on any other type of accessories, such as any belt or holster?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes. He had weapons. He had a small revolver in his belt, but I couldn't see anything else because they started to -- he started to threaten us and he wanted to split the convoy. He said we would have to split, so I couldn't see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What colour was his belt?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Black belt. Okay. Thank you. Now, returning for a moment to that date when you were -- when you said that you were shot. Prior to being shot, you were looking for potatoes. Where were you going to look for potatoes with your friends?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It was two or three houses away from the place we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, what was two or three houses away from the place you were staying? Did you go to a building to get the potatoes or something else?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It was a field.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And was -- was the field enclosed by a fence or wall?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I presume the field -- strike that. The field did not belong to any of the several of you that were going for the potatoes. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No, nobody owned that, because that was not our village. We were from Zhabar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In your village, based upon your knowledge, was it commonplace for farmers or villagers to have firearms, guns?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Which villagers, which farmers do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were there villagers or farmers in the village where you lived?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Once again the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the village where you lived, were there people with fields, or farmers?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: In our village, in Zhabari, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have knowledge of villagers, Kosovo villagers, having firearms to protect their fields?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. Now, at the part of your statement where you talk about the events when you were shot, I believe in the 2001 statement -- in the 2001 statement, it's at page 7, paragraph 1 of the Albanian, page 5, paragraph 4 of the B/C/S, and page 6, paragraph 1 of the English, and I believe that is at -- at paragraph 28 of the new statement. Now, first of all, you did not mention seeing any police officers in your statement of 2001. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I did mention this in my statement of 2001, and the latter one is the same with the previous one, and I'm saying this again, but I don't know why it is not reflected in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, then, that -- that the 2001 statement does not make reference to the seven police officers that you state that you saw outside the church? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Once again the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. When you say you don't know why it is not reflected in the statement, are you referring to the seven police officers that you now state you saw outside the church?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. I responded to the question you made earlier. It was not about the policemen. It was about officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me clear things up. When I use the term "police officers," I am referring to policemen. Maybe I should just use the word "policemen" from here on out. When you say you don't know why it is not reflected in your statement, are you referring to the seven policemen that you now state you saw outside the church?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And again, are you saying that the translator who translated and prepared the statement in 2001 inaccurately recorded what you told the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. I'm saying that the investigator who interviewed me, he was taking down notes. It was not the interpreter who was taking down notes. It was the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are you telling us, then, that -- well, strike that. I don't think I need to go into that. With respect to the seven policemen that you state now that you saw, these policemen were outside the church. That is to say they were not at the top of the church; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes, outside the church, in the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I can take it from your statement that these seven persons, these policemen that you saw, you did not see any of them pointing any guns in your direction. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It is true that I couldn't see whether they were pointing their guns towards me or in our direction, because they were very far away from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact, I think in your statement, in the Albanian -- in the 2001 statement, it's the Albanian page 7, paragraph 1, the B/C/S page 5, paragraph 4, the English page 6, paragraph 1, I think that you confirm in there that you do not know whether in fact the gunmen came from that direction. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. I know where they shot from or where that person shot from, because I was with my back towards the police, and the bullet came from where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, you did not see the individual who fired the gun, did you?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No, I didn't. But when I fell on the ground, I saw other bullets coming from the direction where the police were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You did not -- strike that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You do observe, Mr. Ivetic, that in the statement of 2001 the witness actually says: "I believe there was more than one, because whenever we saw policemen they always were more than only one."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do observe that, Your Honour, and it doesn't seem to clarify things any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, but it indicates a reference to the police being in the vicinity in -- being made in the statement in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh. Well, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But what I'm getting at, ma'am, is that you actually don't know where the shooting was coming from or who was engaged in the shooting. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No. I -- I know where the shots came from and who shot me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How far away is that location from where you were?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: It was quite a distance. I can't give you an exact distance or a number for -- of metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You did not see any muzzle-flash from any weapons, did you?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: No, I couldn't because it was far away, so I couldn't see who exactly was it that shot me. When I got shot, I fell on the ground and I lost consciousness, and for half an hour they continued to shoot in my direction, so much so that nobody could come and pick me up and take me into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you lost consciousness, ma'am, how is it that you saw the bullets and where they were coming from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, I would intervene. I mean, this is not a question to be asked, because the bullet hit her, and thereafter she became unconscious or whatever. She fell down. I mean, this sort of a question is not -- is not appropriate, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, with all due respect, I believe she has testified that after she was shot there was shooting for half an hour and that she saw where those bullets were coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: We are talking of the bullet that hit her. We're not talking of random firing. We're not talking of general firing. We're talk of that bullet firing and she falling down and she seeing it is coming from a direction. I mean, this sort of question -- I'm observing the way things are being asked, but sometimes one has to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can clarify. I'm asking about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: You may clarify. But the way, sir, the questions are being put does bother me because I think we have her statement, we've read her statement, we've seen what she's deposed, and the way things are being questioned over many things, I mean, that calls for interference, although we are not doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Ivetic, you've actually explained there may be some misunderstanding and, therefore, you may proceed to ask questions along the lines you were indicating.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise. The microphone was not on. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, earlier today, at page 41 of the transcript, pages [sic] 2 to 4, I asked you: "Ma'am, you did not see the individual who fired the gun, did you?" And the answer was: "No, I didn't, but when I fell to the ground, I saw other bullets coming from the direction where the police were." And so I'm asking you now, first of all, if you were unconscious, how did you see the other bullets coming from the direction where the police were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think we've yet established exactly when she became unconscious and how long she was unconscious for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we might have done if that question was answered, might we not?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm hoping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Sadiku, the issue that's before us at the moment relates to you becoming unconscious. Can you tell us at what stage you became unconscious?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: After the bullet hit me on my back, for two or three minutes I couldn't understand what was going on. I lost consciousness for two or three minutes. When I was on the ground, I regained consciousness, and I saw -- I touched my body and there was blood, and then I could understand what had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I can imagine that you were -- you were in a state of -- of shock when you were on the ground. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I could also imagine that you perhaps do not remember clearly all the events while you were in this state of distress. Is that also accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: For those two or three minutes. I can't remember what happened during those two or three minutes, but after that I remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. My point is: You did not see any of the seven policemen shooting at you at any point in time. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: I did not see the seven policemen who were in the courtyard. I did not see one of them shooting of me, but I think that there were more -- more than seven policemen there. Not only seven, many more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that belief is based upon your speculation. Isn't that accurate? That is to say, you did not see any more policemen there with your own eyes, did you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, don't answer that question. We're now in a courtyard, Mr. Ivetic, so can you get us, first of all, out of the courtyard and back to the church?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I mean, you're asking questions at cross-purposes with the witness at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, she's -- she's -- I'll ask a question then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you see any police officers -- strike that, policemen. Did you see any policemen in the church?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Inside the church building you saw policemen?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: There were some at the part where the bell of the church is. I don't know what that part of the church is called, but there were some up there, and there were some outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where is that reflected in either your statement of 2001 or your statement of 2006?

utterances.speaker: SADIJE SADIKU
utterances.text: The policemen I saw were in the courtyard of the church, and I'm saying this again. And I am positive that there were not only those policemen that were in the courtyard, but there were others as well. I remembered this later. I remember this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry about that interruption, but there's a fair degree of confusion among the Judges about the questions that have been asked and the answers that are being given, and we've been trying to clarify in our own minds where you have reached, Mr. Ivetic, and I think we've no option but to let you carry on, and you do your best to clarify the point you're trying to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will try, Your Honour, but that will be dependent upon the answers that I receive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Sadiku, in your statement of 2001 and your statement from 2006, I would direct you in your statement of 2001 to the Albanian, page 7, paragraph 1, which in English is the -- page 6, paragraph 1, B/C/S page 5, paragraph 4. In your statement that is being taken as sworn testimony in these proceedings, it is recorded that you state: "From the church in Zablace i Eperm, Upper Zablac, I saw from my position smoke from the top of the church. I do not know if the gunman was there or not but I saw the smoke."
